$comment: Scenario card style spec for scripts/art/cards.mjs. Prompt = subject + lighting + campaign $palette + $style. Subjects marked TODO block paid runs (dry runs still work). Draft: the orchestrator may refine after the C2 pilot.
$style: Painterly realism illustration, cinematic matte-painting key art, fully finished rendering with resolved detail on the subject, no loose sketch or speed-paint brushwork, atmospheric depth, clear value structure with one light direction; not comic, not photographic. 3:2 landscape composition. Horizon line in the lower third of the frame; sky fills at least the upper 60%. One anchor subject placed off-centre on a third of the frame; the subject's base sits near the lower-third line, fully in frame with clear margin on every edge. Calm negative space. No text, no logos, no readable screens, no faces. No people unless the subject names them; when named, at most two distant figures under 5% of frame height, mid-ground, never in the foreground. No fire, smoke, sparks or explosions; any warm accent is one small electric lamp or lit window. Soft film grain, consistent brushwork, cohesive set of scenario cards. Every satellite dish has a solid, opaque reflector with its feed at the focus on struts, and the whole dish stays in frame. No signature, watermark, artist mark or lettering anywhere, including corners. No steam, vapour plumes or smoke; heat is at most a nearly transparent shimmer.

$palette.nats: New England cool blues and granite greys with a single small warm tungsten lamp accent.
$palette.nats-eu: North Atlantic slate, sea-green and amber.

1.title: First Day
1.subject: A nine-metre C-band dish stands on the left third of a Vermont hillside, its clean reflector angled above dew-covered grass. A gravel access path leads toward the pedestal, suggesting the start of a first inspection round.

2.title: Scheduled Maintenance
2.subject: A Vermont C-band dish rests in maintenance position on the right third of the frame, its feed assembly lowered toward an access platform. A work lamp catches disconnected waveguide flanges beneath the motionless reflector.

3.title: Weather Emergency Handover
3.subject: A nine-metre Vermont dish occupies the left third, its reflector collecting heavy snow while wind drives white curtains across the hillside. Ice thickens around the feed support, and the access road nearly disappears into the storm.

4.title: New Bird on the Block
4.subject: A Vermont C-band dish with a solid, opaque painted reflector sits on the right third, caught midway through a broad turn toward a fresh patch of sky. Its open azimuth track and newly displaced wheel marks make the change of pointing visible.

5.title: Interference Hunt
5.subject: A C-band feed horn on its struts at the focus of the Vermont reflector, mouth facing back into the dish, sits on the left third; its paired polarization ports and adjustment collar are sharply defined. A narrow inspection beam from below isolates the assembly against the night sky, with open ground and no structures in the foreground.

6.title: Old Faithful
6.subject: An ageing Vermont antenna pedestal occupies the right third, its weathered elevation gearing exposed beneath the cropped reflector. Fresh grease on the worn drive teeth suggests the repeated small corrections needed to follow a wandering target.

7.title: Uplink Validation
7.subject: A newly serviced feed assembly stands on the left third at the focus of Vermont's C-band reflector, clean waveguide joints contrasting with older painted supports. Closed access covers and neatly secured cables suggest overnight work completed just before uplink validation. The site is empty, with no figures anywhere.

8.title: Night Shift
8.subject: A lone Vermont C-band dish occupies the right third under a deep starless sky, its pedestal washed by a single security lamp. Wet gravel and an empty access platform give the operating antenna an isolated, unattended feeling.

9.title: Morning Rounds
9.subject: The Vermont equipment site occupies the left third beyond a dew-covered fence, its nine-metre C-band dish silhouette rising from low ground mist behind the equipment hut. A freshly opened service gate and warm window glow suggest the first rounds of a newly qualified shift.

10.title: Customer Pass
10.subject: A Vermont C-band dish stands on the right third, its feed aimed steadily into a narrow opening between fast-moving clouds. A nearly transparent heat shimmer above the rear amplifier housing, no visible vapour, steam or plumes suggests a sustained, demanding transmission window.

11.title: Planned Maintenance: Hand Off
11.subject: The Maine coastal dish sits on the left third above a rocky inlet, its reflector tracking steadily out over the grey sea, one warm lit window in the small equipment hut beside it as the station quietly carries another site's traffic.

12.title: Planned Maintenance: Return to Service
12.subject: The Vermont C-band dish stands whole on the right third, its feed horn at the reflector focus showing a replacement waveguide gasket seated between bright, freshly tightened flanges. An empty access cradle hangs below the feed, the antenna poised to return to service; the full reflector and pedestal stay in frame.

13.title: Thermal Anomaly
13.subject: A Vermont dish feed assembly occupies the left third, its rear converter housing surrounded by a nearly transparent heat shimmer with no visible vapour or plume. The cooling grille is packed with dry debris while the surrounding hillside remains still and cool.

14.title: Rain Fade
14.subject: A C-band earth-station dish on a Vermont hillside, a dark rain front sweeping in from the right, a faint, nearly transparent heat shimmer just above the feed housing, no visible vapour or smoke rising into the sky. The dish sits off-centre on the left third of the frame.

15.title: Frequency Coordination
15.subject: A Vermont C-band feed horn sits on the right third, its waveguide filter section and carefully aligned joints visible beneath the reflector. Thin parallel cloud bands beyond the assembly suggest the narrow separation required between neighbouring transmissions.

16.title: Cascade Failure
16.subject: The Vermont equipment site occupies the left third, with uneven amber service light spilling from several open equipment bays. A motionless cooling fan and a nearly transparent heat shimmer beneath the dish suggest several independent faults demanding attention at once.

17.title: Solar Event
17.subject: A Vermont C-band dish stands on the right third in near silhouette, its pointing axis aligned with the low sun directly beyond the feed. A concentrated bright glare washes across the reflector, making the unavoidable solar interference visible.

18.title: Satellite Anomaly
18.subject: A Maine coastal antenna pedestal fills the left third, its elevation drive freshly exposed beneath a weathered C-band reflector. A loosened protective boot and active gearing suggest an unexpected return to continuous tracking above the cold sea.

19.title: Train the New Hire
19.subject: A Vermont C-band dish occupies the right third above a training platform, with two distant mid-ground back-turned figures, each under 5% of frame height, observing its feed alignment. One gestures toward the tracking mechanism while the other watches, turning a familiar procedure into instruction.

20.title: Dual Outage
20.subject: A Vermont C-band feed horn dominates the left third, its heater jacket dark beneath a thick shell of rime ice. Wind-driven sleet streaks past the frozen aperture as the winter front consumes the hillside behind it.

21.title: Hostile RF
21.subject: A large satellite dish on its pedestal (the dish itself carries no lights) pointed at a low sky, with a distant unfamiliar mast and a single faint red beacon on the ridge line in the direction the dish is aimed. The mood is quiet tension. The dish sits on the right third of the frame.

22.title: End-of-Life Planning
22.subject: An ageing Vermont C-band dish stands on the right third, its patched reflector and faded protective coating catching weak light. Fallen leaves gather around the pedestal, giving the still-operating antenna the quiet gravity of a final assessment.

23.title: Emergency Bypass
23.subject: A Vermont antenna pedestal occupies the left third, its local manual-control compartment open beneath a stationary reflector. A portable work light reveals intact servo hardware and a disconnected controller module, suggesting movement remains possible despite failed automation.

24.title: Constellation Crisis
24.subject: The Vermont equipment site occupies the right third beneath an advancing wall of storm cloud, its operating dish sharply outlined against the last clear sky. Loose gravel and bent grass reveal the first gusts reaching an already pressured station.

1.title: First Light Over Galway
1.subject: A Ku-band LEO tracking dish on a green Galway headland, tilted toward a low pale sky, a small radome building beside it and a drystone wall in the foreground, the Atlantic beyond. The dish sits on the left third of the frame.

2.title: Proving the Link
2.subject: A Galway Ku-band tracking dish occupies the right third, its precisely aligned reflector framed against a clear gap in layered Atlantic cloud. A temporary calibration fixture on the feed support suggests a station still being measured against its promised performance.

3.title: Two-Way Street
3.subject: A Galway Ku-band feed assembly occupies the left third, its newly connected transmit waveguide catching warm light beneath the reflector. Fresh weatherproofing around the uplink housing suggests a receive station preparing to send its first authenticated command.

4.title: Keys to the Bird
4.subject: The Galway equipment site sits on the right third, its secured service entrance illuminated beside a closed, windowless communications enclosure. Fresh tamper seals and protected cable conduits suggest controlled access to the machinery behind a trusted command link.

5.title: Shetland Comes Online
5.subject: A newly commissioned Ku-band dish stands on the left third of a Shetland headland, its pale reflector above wind-flattened grass. Fresh foundation gravel contrasts with dark peat and sea spray, suggesting a remote station finally joining the network.

6.title: Watch the Watchers
6.subject: The Galway equipment site occupies the left third behind a wet perimeter fence, its access gate closed beneath a sharply defined security light. An empty service path and long fence shadows give an ordinary inspection an unusually watchful atmosphere.

7.title: Moving Target
7.subject: A Galway tracking pedestal occupies the right third, its curved cable carrier stretched into a newly changed azimuth position. An older arc of scuffed gravel beneath the drive contrasts with the fresh direction of the reflector overhead.

8.title: Night Passes
8.subject: A Galway Ku-band dish occupies the left third beneath broken cloud, its reflector turning above a dark radome building. One small pool of maintenance light on the empty headland suggests a solo operator carrying an entire night's pass schedule.

9.title: Morning Constellation
9.subject: The Galway equipment site sits on the right third above a misty Atlantic inlet, with its tracking dish already raised from stow. Pale light catches dew on the perimeter fence as a busy day of constellation contacts begins.

10.title: Priority Tasking
10.subject: A Galway Ku-band dish occupies the left third, tipped low toward a thin strip of sea beneath heavy cloud, the headland rising close on either side so the narrow pass window feels tight.

11.title: LEOP: Launch Day
11.subject: A Galway Ku-band dish stands on the right third, its reflector searching just above an empty Atlantic horizon. A wide expanse of pale sky surrounds the small antenna, suggesting the uncertainty of acquiring a spacecraft on its first orbit.

12.title: LEOP: Commissioning
12.subject: A Galway Ku-band feed horn occupies the left third, its newly fitted calibration coupler and immaculate connectors visible beneath the reflector. A temporary protective cover lies folded against the support, suggesting final acceptance work before operational imagery delivery.

13.title: The Numbers Don't Lie
13.subject: A Galway Ku-band dish occupies the right third, tilted almost vertically with its elevation mechanism close to the zenith limit. Weather staining around the feed housing adds a second visible concern to the difficult overhead tracking geometry.

14.title: Atlantic Low
14.subject: A Galway Ku-band dish stands on the left third as dense rain turns to sleet across the headland. Meltwater runs from the heated feed cover while a dark Atlantic cloud shelf closes over the reflector's low pointing direction.

15.title: Rotation Day
15.subject: The Galway equipment site occupies the right third, its antenna lowered between contacts beside a securely closed communications shelter. A narrow break in racing clouds briefly illuminates the service entrance, suggesting a short interval for a coordinated security change.

16.title: Cascade
16.subject: A Shetland antenna pedestal occupies the left third, its cooling compartment open beneath a steeply raised Ku-band reflector. A single distant mid-ground back-turned technician, under 5% of frame height, leans toward the stalled fan while wind strains the loose access cover.

17.title: Unusual Activity
17.subject: The Galway equipment site sits on the left third, its quiet radome and closed entrance reflected in rain-dark paving. A security lamp leaves the outer fence in shadow, suggesting subtle activity beyond an otherwise routine overnight watch.

18.title: Dirty Spectrum
18.subject: A Galway Ku-band feed horn occupies the right third, exposed beneath a dry reflector while a distant rain band remains offshore. An attached diagnostic coupler suggests repeated interference checks under weather that cannot explain the persistent degradation.

19.title: Frequency Agility
19.subject: A Galway Ku-band feed assembly occupies the left third, with its compact tuning housing and protected RF connections clearly visible. Fast-moving cloud shadows cross the reflector, suggesting the need to keep a command path usable as conditions change.

20.title: False Time
20.subject: The sky above Galway fills the frame, with a fading star field confined to the right third over a low coastal silhouette. Faint doubled star trails suggest a trusted timing reference slipping away from the true sky.

21.title: Knocking on the Door
21.subject: The Galway equipment site occupies the right third, its communications shelter sealed behind a secondary locked solid steel barrier. A narrow shaft of light reaches the protected cable entry, concentrating attention on the boundary guarding the command path.

22.title: Connecting the Dots
22.subject: The Galway equipment site sits on the left third, viewed from outside where antenna foundations, protected conduits and perimeter fencing converge. Receding cloud reveals the whole installation clearly, suggesting separate incidents finally understood as one connected pattern.

23.title: Dark Passes
23.subject: A Galway tracking pedestal occupies the right third beneath a barely visible reflector, its normal service lights extinguished. A single portable lamp illuminates the manual-control compartment, suggesting one essential command must survive a night of simultaneous failures.

24.title: North Atlantic Storm
24.subject: A tracking dish and a small equipment hut on a storm-lashed Atlantic headland, sleet slanting across the frame, waves breaking on dark rocks, one warm lit window in the hut. The dish sits on the right third of the frame.

25.title: Site Orientation
25.subject: The Galway equipment site occupies the left third beyond an open pedestrian gate, with a clear inspection path following the fence toward the radome. The empty route suggests the start of a deliberate review of the station's defences.

26.title: Baseline Check
26.subject: A Galway antenna pedestal occupies the right third, its inspection cover open to reveal one conspicuously fresh cable among older, neatly secured runs. Cool condensation on the housing suggests a pre-pass check catching an unexplained configuration change.

27.title: Removable Media
27.subject: A Galway antenna pedestal occupies the left third, its controller service compartment open with a small removable drive still inserted in the maintenance port. An unattended tool roll rests below, suggesting an unverified firmware transfer interrupted before installation.

28.title: Vendor Session
28.subject: The Galway equipment site sits on the right third, its maintenance-room window unexpectedly lit while the tracking dish remains stowed. The locked gate and empty access road suggest remote activity occurring without an authorised visit.
